sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM as stated; the EVENT itself Unverified] The IRGC Navy said two oil tankers struck naval mines in/near the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire, were badly damaged and stopped moving. The vessels had switched off their tracking systems and were using what the IRGC called an unauthorised route. The announcement came at 20:56 GMT Nov 7, 21 minutes after CENTCOM disabled the St Kitts-flagged M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman (20:35 GMT). [OVERLAP WARNING -- DO NOT COUNT AS A SECOND INCIDENT] This claim matches, in wording and detail (tracking switched off, unauthorised route, fire, stopped), the IRGC claim already recorded at totw-20261107-1000-04 (ABNA, published 04:49Z Nov 7, 'two more oil tankers halted after striking mines'). It is likely the SAME claim re-announced/reported in the evening, not a second pair of tankers; no vessel name, flag, position or casualty figure distinguishes the two reports. The Nov 5 claim (five tankers + a tug) and the Nov 7 early-morning single-tanker claim (1700-01) are separate earlier items. [PORTWATCH -- STALE] Newest snapshot portwatch-2026-11-08.json, fetched 03:06 , stale=true (latest observation 2026-11-01, lag 7 days): Hormuz counted 1 transit on Nov 1, 7-day average 4.43 vs 2025 baseline 85.53/day (5.2% of baseline). No fresh counted transit figure exists; the IRGC's claim is NOT a counted figure.
sections.what_verified: Primary-source single family: the claim originates with the IRGC Navy alone. AJ (T2), NDTV Profit (T3) and Times of Israel (T3) relay the same IRGC statement -- relays of one primary source do not add families.
sections.what_disputed: No independent confirmation from maritime officials, UKMTO, vessel operators or insurers; the Roya/Sepah footage circulating with the claim is from the Nov 1 mine claim, not verified as this incident. The 21-minute gap to the Huda disabling is timing, not evidence of coordination -- the two actions were by rival commands under competing legal frameworks. CENTCOM's own tally (147 vessels redirected, 5 disabled, 10 tankers destroyed, $25bn crude blocked since July) is the US side's claimant figure, equally unverified as a counted total.
sections.why_matters: Same day, same water, both sides hit ships -- but the IRGC's 'two tankers' may be the morning's claim told twice. The counted number that matters is still missing.
sections.context: Background: UPDATE TO totw-20261107-1000-04 (ABNA 04:49Z Nov 7, two tankers) -- IN-WINDOW re-report (NDTV Profit published 2026-11-08T07:40:36+05:30 = 06:10 ; AJ liveblog updated 00:07:40Z) -- IRGC Navy says two oil tankers hit sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire, 21 minutes after CENTCOM disabled M/V Huda; no independent confirmation, no vessel names

totw_analysis: Our read: Same day, same water, both sides hit ships -- but the IRGC's 'two tankers' may be the morning's claim told twice. The counted number that matters is still missing. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Are the mine claims real shipping warfare or a blockade-evasion deterrent story -- and who do you believe when neither side shows you the ship?
